findings.document_value: $100 copayment per ER visit; waived if held for observation or admitted within 24 hours; out-of-network same as in-network
findings.note: Cross-confirmed by a second document: SMB p.6 independently states the identical figure ('$100 copayment (waived if admitted)', 'no deductible' out-of-network) -- BD and SMB agree here, unlike the Rx-supply-limit conflict below.

This fact isn't in the Benefit Description's Schedule of Benefits at all (no distinct 'Urgent Care' line item there) -- it only exists in the Summary of Medical Benefits, matching the plan profile's own citation choice (SMB, not BD) for this slot.

findings.document_value: $100 copayment per admission at most network hospitals; $500 at Hospital Choice Cost Sharing higher-tier hospitals
findings.note: Cross-confirmed by SMB p.6 ('$100 copayment per admission at lower-cost-share hospitals, $500 at higher-cost-share hospitals') -- BD and SMB agree. The specific higher-tier hospital list (HCCS rider) was not checked in this run -- the profile itself flags that rider as unattached to the posted 2026 PDF.

findings.document_value: No charge for first 8 visits per plan year, then $35 copayment per visit; 30% after deductible out-of-network
findings.note: Website and document describe different dimensions, not a contradiction: the website confirms there's no cap on the NUMBER of visits, the document (BD SoB p.5, cross-confirmed SMB p.6) states the COST-SHARE per visit. Both are true simultaneously. Resolves the ambiguity the first pass flagged.

findings.website_value: "Copayments for prescriptions purchased at a retail pharmacy are up to a 30-day supply." — matches BD, not SMB.
findings.document_value: BD Schedule of Benefits: 30-day retail supply (confirmed directly in the PDF: '(30-day supply†)' with a footnote limiting certain drugs to 30 days). SMB: 'up to a 60-day formulary supply for each prescription or refill' -- but SMB's own footnote 5 concedes 'Certain medications limited to 30-day supply,' which softens the conflict from a flat 30-vs-60 disagreement to SMB stating a looser general rule with an internal exception that may cover most of the formulary.
findings.note: Website sides with BD. Reading SMB's own footnote 5 directly (not just the headline 60-day figure) narrows this from 'two documents flatly disagree' to 'SMB's general rule and footnote may not even disagree with BD once you read past the table' -- still worth a human resolving with HUSHP Member Services, per the plan profile's own open_items, but less alarming than the first pass suggested.

findings.website_value: Routine vision exam: no copay mentioned. Non-routine vision exam: $35 copayment in-network, 30% coinsurance out-of-network.
findings.document_value: Directly confirmed in the BD PDF text (not just the plan profile's transcription): under 'Routine vision care' > 'Routine vision exams (one exam per member per plan year)': '$35 copayment per visit' in-network, '30% after deductible' out-of-network. There is no separate 'non-routine vision exam' line item anywhere in the Schedule of Benefits.
findings.note: Upgraded from the first pass's 'possible stale citation' framing: this is now a primary-source-confirmed contradiction, not just the plan profile's word against the website's. The document explicitly labels the $35 exam 'routine' and has no 'non-routine' exam category at all -- the website's framing appears to simply be wrong, not a citation problem on our side.

needs_slot.website_value: CVS Caremark (named for out-of-network pharmacy paper-claim reimbursement)
needs_slot.note: Read the full BD pharmacy section (SoB p.6 and body pp.51-54, PDF pages 68-71) directly -- no PBM subcontractor is named anywhere; only 'Blue Cross and Blue Shield' and bluecrossma.org are referenced. This independently confirms the plan profile's own caveat that the PBM isn't documented. The website may be the only public source naming it.

needs_slot.website_value: 50% coinsurance for antimalarial drugs (Malarone, Mefloquine, Coartem, Primaquine)
needs_slot.document_value: "Note: There are certain drugs that are used only for the treatment of malaria. For these covered drugs, you will pay 50% (instead of your applicable copayment)."
needs_slot.note: Now document-confirmed, not just website-only. Distinct tier structure from the standard Rx tiers; no existing slot covers it.

needs_slot.website_value: $0 copayment for prescription contraceptive products that are generic or brand name
needs_slot.document_value: "Your cost share will be waived for generic birth control drugs and methods (or for a brand-name drug or method when a generic is not available or not medically appropriate for you)..."
needs_slot.note: Reclassified from the first pass: initially looked like the website might be overstating the waiver (profile's SoB footnote only mentions Tier-1/generic). Reading body p.53 directly shows the website is accurate -- brand-name IS waived, conditionally on medical necessity, a nuance the website omits but doesn't contradict. Still needs its own slot since neither the SoB footnote nor a single existing fact captures the full rule.

needs_slot.website_value: No visit limit, in and out-of-network combined
needs_slot.document_value: Neither BD nor SMB states an explicit overall visit cap for outpatient mental health -- both describe only the per-visit cost-share structure (first 8 free, then $35/30%).
needs_slot.note: Document doesn't contradict the website's claim, but doesn't affirmatively state 'no limit' either -- it's simply silent on a cap. Distinct dimension from the existing mental_health_outpatient cost-share slot; still needs its own slot to be gradable on its own terms rather than inferred from silence.
